data_card.measured: Water levels at seven level meters in the Bellinge combined sewer (Odense, Denmark) through eight storms between 2011 and 2019, read at one minute.
data_card.method: Utility level meters (DTU Data item 2, CC BY 4.0); each meter reads no lower than its own floor.
data_card.uncertainty: Provisional ±0.02 m level-meter accuracy (reference.uncertainty); the published model is uncalibrated (Pedersen et al. 2021, §4).
known_issues: The model is the published, uncalibrated SWMM model run unchanged.
Rain-gauge data (item 3a) are CC BY-NC and not used; the model's own rain-gauge file drives the runs.
Basin and pump-sump meters are dominated by controls the model may not reproduce.
data_card.exercises: Network routing under real storms with basins, pumps, weirs and control rules.
data_card.cannot_tell: With the model run unchanged, the miss against the meters mostly measures the model and its data; the engines agree with each other far better than with the meters.

validation_design.holdout_policy: Engine validation scores every storm because nothing is tuned. A practice-validation round on the same data will use the four storms of 2011–2013 for calibration and score the four of 2014–2019; that split is fixed here, before any practice-validation run.

title: Bellinge combined sewer system (Odense, Denmark) — field validation
description: 1.7 km² mainly combined urban drainage system in Bellinge, Odense, with a published EPA SWMM model and years of level-meter records. A candidate runs the published model, unchanged except for its run dates, on eight storms (2011-2019) and is judged against the measured water levels at seven level meters.

citations.title: The Bellinge data set: open data and models for community-wide urban drainage systems research
Dataset for Bellinge: An urban drainage case study

provenance.adaptation_notes: Uses only CC BY 4.0 items: 7 – Models (SWMM; its rain-gauge file drives the runs) and 2 – Sensor data. Item 3a (rain gauges) is CC BY-NC 4.0 and is not used; the radar (3b) is not needed. The published SWMM model is uncalibrated (ESSD paper §4), so this case judges the model and the engine together. Storms: the eight most intense in the model's rain-gauge series after the level meters start (Aug 2010), including the model's own 29 June 2012 event.

uncertainty.notes: Provisional level-meter accuracy. Each meter reads no lower than its own floor (the lowest level it recorded in any of the storms); the scorer reads the model the same way.

criteria.rationale: Set before any run: Moriasi et al. (2007) 'satisfactory' band, NSE ≥ 0.5, for the median gauge record (a meter on one storm). A record where the meter moved less than three times its accuracy is not scored for NSE.

significance.source: Moriasi et al. (2007), Model evaluation guidelines for systematic quantification of accuracy in watershed simulations, Trans. ASABE 50(3)
significance.basis: Lower bound of the 'satisfactory' band for NSE.

criteria.rationale: Set before any run: the ±0.1 m depth criterion for verifying sewer models against measurements (WaPUG 2002; CIWEM UDG 2017 Code of Practice), for the median gauge record.

significance.source: WaPUG (2002) Code of Practice for the Hydraulic Modelling of Sewer Systems; CIWEM UDG (2017) Code of Practice for the Hydraulic Modelling of Urban Drainage Systems
significance.basis: Depth criterion for verifying a sewer model against measured event levels.
